body: @heycam @tabatkins any suggestions? Can we reference SVG2 yet?

> Can we reference SVG2 yet?

Judging by https://github.com/whatwg/platform.html5.org/commit/f1f9bd1d8325d585d2295986e17aba2d632fdd07 , no.

Ignoring vendor support for new features in SVG 2, I am sure vendors are interested in more precise definitions of existing features, which is something SVG 2 also aims to provide.  Still, I wouldn't reference it just yet -- half the spec is still in a bit of a state.  Let's re-evaluate once we get the spec to CR (aiming for around February 2016 currently).

I think the responsible thing to do would be to make a note of the mess and talk a bit about which parts of each spec to reference. But it's not too high priority since in theory the problem will solve itself in ~5 months, modulo the planning fallacy.
Removing any reference to 1.2 is a good thing to do _right now_; that spec has never been anything but fiction on the web.  Noting the few things that are brought in from Tiny would be good, tho.

Preliminary research on SVG implementations:

---

**Stuff unimplemented in 1.1 and friends**
- [`externalResourcesRequired`](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#ExternalResourcesRequiredAttribute) used to be [in Chrome](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#ExternalResourcesRequiredAttribute), was [never in IE](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ff934780%28v=vs.85%29.aspx), [wontfix in Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=277955), and [is probably still in WebKit](http://trac.webkit.org/browser/trunk/Source/WebCore/svg/SVGExternalResourcesRequired.h). Unpopular [in the spec](https://github.com/whatwg/html/commit/068eaf4560aef0447f54201b552808ef6c64359c), too.
- [`enable-background`](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/filters.html#EnableBackgroundProperty) died a death from being poorly specified and Adobe Illustrator polluting all of its exported SVGs with it, whether they needed them or not. [Only Presto implemented it](http://www.opera.com/docs/specs/presto25/svg/cssproperties/).
- `xml:space` has weird problems across browsers, and [IE doesn't care at all](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/gg557993%28v=vs.85%29.aspx), but that's okay because nobody wants [its bizarre specced behavior](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/text.html#WhiteSpace). Superseded by CSS `white-space`.
- [Browsers don't like `<tref>`](http://tavmjong.free.fr/SVG/TREF/tref.html), only supported in Blink.
- SVG Fonts [used to be supported in many browsers](http://caniuse.com/#feat=svg-fonts), but are obsoleted in favor of CSS `font-face` because [they cannot have hinting](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/fonts.html#SVGFontsOverview). [The font-defining elements](www.w3.org/TR/SVG/fonts.html), [`<altGlyph>`](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/text.html#AltGlyphElement), [`<altGlyphDef>`, `<altGlyphItem>`, and `<glyphRef>`](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/text.html#AlternateGlyphDefinitions) are deprecated and [aren't in the main SVG2 spec](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/eltindex.html). (I think they got moved to a module, so perhaps they're not dead; only sleeping.) IE never bothered with any of them.
- SMIL animations were never implemented in IE (well, [not for SVG](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms533099%28v=vs.85%29.aspx), anyway) and are being removed from Blink.
- `<animateColor>` is redundant. [Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=436296), [Chrome](https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=332839).
- [The color profile/rendering elements and attributes](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/color.html#ColorProfileDescriptions) are a no-go in browsers ([Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=427713), [IE](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ff934705%28v=vs.85%29.aspx),. They're useful for print-focused programs, though.
- [Firefox does not implement the `<cursor>` element](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=177193), and [neither does IE](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ff934779%28v=vs.85%29.aspx). Not a big problem, use CSS instead.
- The XLink properties other than `href`, `title`, and `show` (equivalents to HTML's `href`, `title`, and `target`) are unsupported. (No big surprise.)
- `zoomAndPan` has never been supported, [aside from standard browser UI & functionality](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ff934700%28v=vs.85%29.aspx) for zooming and panning across web pages. I remember Presto trying something with it, but alas.
- Text baseline stuff is [weird](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=308338) or [unsupported](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/gg558060%28v=vs.85%29.aspx) across browsers and best avoided at present.
- `version` and `baseProfile` never did anything.
- `contentScriptType` and `contentStyleType` were largely unnecessary and browsers saw no point in implementing them.
- [IE doesn't implement the `normalizedPathSegList` or `pathLength` DOM interfaces.](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/gg558089%28v=vs.85%29.aspx) Considering how much of SVG's DOM is, uh, creative, can't say I blame them.

---

**Stuff implemented from Tiny 1.2**
- [Chrome has the `<discard>` element.](https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=327339) It's less about animation and more about removing unneeded resources, I think.
- [Chrome used to have `bufferedRendering`](https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=330420#c14), but they're removing it [in favor of `will-change`](http://www.w3.org/2014/04/08-svg-minutes.html#action02). (Presto used to have it, too.) Shame, because I don't think `will-change` has a value for "I won't get animated much." Perhaps that's what the `scroll-position` value does?
- [IE9+ implemented Tiny's interactivity module.](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/bg124137%28v=vs.85%29.aspx)
- [WebKit](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=31438), [Chrome](https://code.google.com/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=497498), and [Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=528332) support `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`. So did Presto.
- All browsers let you use and manipulate `class` attributes on elements that aren't allowed to have them in 1.1, but that's like how they let you do that for all the elements in HTML 4.01 that weren't allowed to have it either.
- Ditto ARIA's `role`. Supposedly you can use it in 1.1 with XML's extensibility features, but who would?
- Apparently [Tiny's resizing in CSS contexts makes more sense](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=597272), but last I checked the whole situation is an utter mess anyway. The padding-box hack lives.
- Tiny's error handling is a de facto standard, because draconian error handling is terrible.

---

While I'm here, does anybody know if the HTML inside SVG's HTML-integration points is supposed to be parsed as tag-soup, or foreign content?

@Tigt this is really impressive stuff. Would you be up for shaping that up into a pull request? For each item you'd want to make a decision as to what the spec should say, e.g. if two browsers don't implement it and it's a redundant feature anyway, then the HTML spec should say "don't implement it." Whereas if two browsers don't implement it but that's just because they haven't caught up, we can leave it out.

Here is a quick sample of how I would do things. In https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#svg-0, I would insert something like:

**User agent requirements**. SVG as implemented in user agents today follows neither _SVG 1.1_ nor _SVG Tiny 1.2_ precisely, but instead subsets of each. Although it is hoped that the in-progress _SVG 2_ specification will give a more realistic target for implementations, until that specification is ready, user agents must implement the _SVG 1.1_ specification with the following willful violations and additions. [SVG11] [SVGTiny12] [SVG2]

The following features from SVG 1.1 must not be implemented:
- The externalResourcesRequired attribute
- The enable-background property
- The xml:space attribute (use CSS's white-space property instead)
- ...

The following features from SVG Tiny 1.2 must be implemented:
- The "non-scaling-stroke" value for the vector-effect property
- ...

Feel free to change any of my suggestions to be more accurate or complete or go down a different path or whatever. But I'd really love to capture the work you've done in the spec for implementers and authors to refer to.

Quick note on this:

> The xml:space attribute (use CSS's white-space property instead)

xml:space is needed for compatibility with content, however the way it is implemented/supported changed in SVG 2.  It is now meant to be implemented through a UA style sheet rule that maps it to the white-space property: https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/styling.html#UAStyleSheet

I would say don't mention SMIL until we get a majority of browser vendors indicating one way or another; right now it's evenly split.

I don't really know the answer to the content model question :-/.

As for getting set up, try the instructions at https://github.com/whatwg/html-build ? Feel free to open issues there with any particular issues. Alternately you could try writing things up in text or Markdown first to get some review on the contents without worrying about the syntax and Git stuff.
